arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Draper represented Kansas. He argued the case returned after the 1995 violation finding. He focused on the Master's proposed remedy.
Mr. Robbins represented Colorado. He cited North Dakota v. Minnesota. He argued the Court should limit the remedy to an injunction.
Mr. Minear represented the United States. He argued the damages calculation does not violate the Eleventh Amendment. He supported allowing prejudgment interest on a discretionary basis.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: Kansas sued Colorado over water rights. The Court found Colorado violated the compact in 1995. The case returned to a Special Master for damages. Kansas now seeks prejudgment interest. Colorado opposes this specific remedy. The United States supports allowing interest.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines how states calculate compensation for water compact breaches. It sets the standard for financial remedies in interstate disputes. It clarifies the scope of the Eleventh Amendment in these suits.
